title: DOGE | Elon Musk's Quest to Shrink the US Government
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇妙而有趣的事物，同时提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about DOGE, the Department of Governmental Efficiency.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们将探讨 DOGE，即政府效率部。

sentences.en: It was established by Executive Order on Donald Trump’s first day back in office and has been plagued by controversy ever since.
sentences.zh: 它是在唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫的第一天通过行政令成立的，自此以后便争议不断。

sentences.en: So, in this episode, we’ll look at what it did, what it still does, why it is loved and loathed in almost equal measure, and ask ourselves what happens next.
sentences.zh: 因此，在本期节目中，我们将探讨它做了什么、它仍在做什么、为什么它让人又爱又恨，并自问接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and talk about DOGE.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们言归正传，聊聊 DOGE。

sentences.en: On Saturday, 22nd February, earlier this year, millions of American federal employees got the same email.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候的 2 月 22 日星期六，数百万美国联邦雇员收到了同一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: It was, on one level, a simple request. It asked them to list five things that they achieved that week.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，这是一个简单的要求。它要求他们列出那周完成的五项工作。

sentences.en: They shouldn’t disclose any classified information, and simple bullet points were fine.
sentences.zh: 他们不应泄露任何机密信息，简单的要点即可。

sentences.en: The email came from the OPM, the Office of Personnel Management, which is the US government’s human resources agency.
sentences.zh: 这封邮件来自 OPM，即美国人事管理局，它是美国政府的人力资源机构。

sentences.en: However, a quick glance at social media revealed the ultimate source of the email and the potential consequences of not responding.
sentences.zh: 然而，大致浏览一下社交媒体就会发现这封邮件的最终来源以及不回复的潜在后果。

sentences.en: At 8.30 pm that evening, Elon Musk posted on X, “Consistent with President @realDonaldTrump’s instructions, all federal employees will shortly receive an email requesting to understand what they got done last week.
sentences.zh: 当天晚上 8 点 30 分，Elon Musk 在 X 上发帖称：“根据总统 @realDonaldTrump 的指示，所有联邦雇员将很快收到一封电子邮件，要求了解他们上周完成了什么工作。

sentences.en: Failure to respond will be taken as a resignation.”
sentences.zh: 不予回复将被视为辞职。”

sentences.en: This was just over a month into the establishment of DOGE, the Department of Governmental Efficiency, and was one of its most controversial acts.
sentences.zh: 这发生在 DOGE（政府效率部）成立一个多月后，是其最具争议的行为之一。

sentences.en: To some, it was a perfectly fair request.
sentences.zh: 在有些人看来，这是一个完全合理的要求。

sentences.en: These were federal employees, people whose salaries are paid by taxpayers, so they should be answerable to the public.
sentences.zh: 这些是联邦雇员，他们的薪水由纳税人支付，因此他们应该对公众负责。

sentences.en: And this was hardly a difficult question to answer: list five things they did that week.
sentences.zh: 而且这几乎不是一个难回答的问题：列出他们那周做的五项工作。

sentences.en: To others, it was a crude, politically-charged request, an act of intimidation dressed up as accountability, less about measuring productivity and more about reminding people who held the power.
sentences.zh: 但在另一些人看来，这是一个粗暴的、带有政治色彩的要求，是一种伪装成问责制的恐吓行为，与其说是衡量生产力，不如说是提醒人们谁拥有权力。

sentences.en: And there was immediate confusion among federal employees, the government workers who received the email.
sentences.zh: 收到邮件的联邦雇员也就是政府工作人员中立刻产生了困惑。

sentences.en: Should they respond? What would happen if they didn’t?
sentences.zh: 他们应该回复吗？如果不回复会怎么样？

sentences.en: Some heads of federal agencies instructed their employees not to respond, others instructed them to respond, others to respond, but to their direct manager, not to the original email.
sentences.zh: 一些联邦机构的负责人指示他们的员工不要回复，另一些人则指示他们回复，还有人指示他们回复，但要发给他们的直接经理，而不是发给原始邮件。

sentences.en: Later that week, it was reported that around 1 million federal employees had responded to the email, but that still left around 1.5 million who had not.
sentences.zh: 那周晚些时候据报道，大约有 100 万联邦雇员回复了邮件，但这仍然意味着大约有 150 万人没有回复。

sentences.en: One of those who did respond was the White House Press Secretary, Karoline Leavitt.
sentences.zh: 白宫新闻秘书 Karoline Leavitt 就是回复的人之一。

sentences.en: She proudly declared that she had responded, saying, “I do five things in about 10 minutes, and all federal workers should be working at the same pace that President Trump is working and moving.
sentences.zh: 她自豪地宣称自己已经回复了，并说道：“我在大约 10 分钟内完成了五件事，所有联邦员工都应该以与特朗普总统相同的工作和推进节奏来工作。

sentences.en: We have a country to save, and we want this federal government to be responsive to the needs of the American people.”
sentences.zh: 我们有一个国家要去拯救，我们希望这个联邦政府能够对美国人民的需求做出回应。”

sentences.en: The message was clear: to “Make America Great Again”, lazy federal employees needed to pick up the pace, and the waste and inefficiency that had been tolerated under previous administrations, both Democratic and Republican, was no longer going to cut the mustard.
sentences.zh: 信息很明确：为了“让美国再次伟大”，懒散的联邦雇员需要加快步伐，而历届政府（无论是民主党还是共和党）一直容忍的浪费和低效将不再管用。

sentences.en: America needed to be saved, and everyone had to pull their weight.
sentences.zh: 美国需要被拯救，每个人都必须尽自己的一份力。

sentences.en: Now, before we get to the question of how much waste and inefficiency there is thought to have been, and some theories about the motivations behind the organisation set up to combat it, we must go back to the start, to well before January 20th, the day that Donald Trump was inaugurated for his second term.
sentences.zh: 现在，在我们探讨人们认为存在多少浪费和低效，以及关于为打击这些现象而设立的组织的动机的一些理论之前，我们必须回到最初，回到 1 月 20 日（唐纳德·特朗普宣誓就职第二任期的日子）之前很久。

sentences.en: In fact, we need to go all the way back to before Trump even became the Republican nominee for the 2024 election.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们需要一直追溯到特朗普甚至还未成为 2024 年大选共和党总统候选人之前。

sentences.en: In September 2023, when multiple candidates were still vying for the Republican nomination, a fundraising dinner was held at a former Facebook executive’s Silicon Valley mansion.
sentences.zh: 2023 年 9 月，当多位候选人仍在争夺共和党提名时，在前 Facebook 高管的硅谷豪宅举行了一场筹款晚宴。

sentences.en: It was a $50,000-a-head fundraiser, raising money for the campaign of the former healthcare entrepreneur, Vivek Ramaswamy.
sentences.zh: 这是一场每人 50,000 美元的筹款活动，旨在为前医疗保健企业家 Vivek Ramaswamy 的竞选活动筹集资金。

sentences.en: Elon Musk was one of the guests. As the evening went on, Musk started musing on the idea of radically reducing the size of the federal government.
sentences.zh: Elon Musk 是嘉宾之一。随着夜渐深，Musk 开始沉思彻底缩减联邦政府规模的想法。

sentences.en: He had bought Twitter a year earlier and had embarked on a radical cost-cutting mission, culling more than 80% of the staff.
sentences.zh: 他一年前收购了 Twitter，并着手进行激进的削减成本任务，裁掉了 80% 以上的员工。

sentences.en: Despite the cries from critics that this would be the end of Twitter, that Musk didn’t have the relevant experience with consumer software or social media to make it a success, Twitter — since rebranded as X — didn’t die a painful death.
sentences.zh: 尽管批评人士叫嚷这将是 Twitter 的末日，Musk 并没有运营消费软件或社交软件的相关经验来取得成功，但 Twitter（后来更名为 X）并没有痛苦地死去。

sentences.en: A flood of advertisers did leave, and it has had its fair share of growing pains, but it actually has more active users now than it did before Elon Musk bought it.
sentences.zh: 大量广告商确实离开了，它也有过成长中的烦恼，但现在它的活跃用户实际上比 Elon Musk 买下它之前还要多。

sentences.en: Musk theorised that he could embark on the same extreme cost-cutting measures at a governmental level.
sentences.zh: Musk 推测，他可以在政府层面采取同样的极端降本增效措施。

sentences.en: And just think of the savings to be made.
sentences.zh: 想想能够节省多少钱。

sentences.en: Twitter might not have been the most efficient company, but it was surely much more efficient than any government.
sentences.zh: Twitter 可能不是最高效的公司，但它肯定比任何政府都要高效得多。

sentences.en: And the numbers were vastly different: Twitter had 8,000 or so employees, the federal government had around 3 million.
sentences.zh: 而且数字截然不同：Twitter 有大约 8,000 名员工，而联邦政府大约有 300 万名。

sentences.en: It was a different scale, a less efficient and vastly larger beast, and all of these savings could be passed right back to the American people.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不同的规模，一个效率低下且庞大得多的庞然大物，所有这些节省下来的资金都可以直接返还给美国人民。

sentences.en: This wasn’t a political challenge, a question of persuading congressmen and women to support the cuts at a political level.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个政治挑战，不是一个说服国会议员在政治层面支持削减开支的问题。

sentences.en: It was a technological challenge, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是一个技术挑战。

sentences.en: Give me access to the systems, let me in, and I will find the waste and cut it.
sentences.zh: 给我访问系统的权限，让我进去，我会找出浪费并将其削减。

sentences.en: Now, Musk never officially supported Ramaswamy, and early the following year, he dropped out of the Republican nomination race and officially pledged support to Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 如今，Musk 从未官方支持过 Ramaswamy，第二年初，他退出了共和党总统提名竞选，并正式表态支持唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: On July 13th, 2024, the same day as the attempted assassination, Elon Musk publicly tweeted out his support for Donald Trump’s presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 2024 年 7 月 13 日，也就是暗杀未遂的同一天，Elon Musk 在公开推特上表达了他对唐纳德·特朗普总统竞选的支持。

sentences.en: As you will remember, Musk ended up becoming Trump’s largest financial backer, spending $290 million to help Donald Trump win re-election.
sentences.zh: 正如你所记得的，Musk 最终成为了特朗普最大的资金支持者，花费 2.90 亿美元帮助唐纳德·特朗普赢得连任。

sentences.en: This isn’t the time to speculate about his motivations for this, but before long, the two men appeared to be joined at the hip.
sentences.zh: 现在不是推测他这样做的动机的时候，但不久之后，这两个人似乎就形影不离了。

sentences.en: And one of Trump’s campaign pledges was to bring in Elon Musk to lead a task force aimed at reducing government spending.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的竞选承诺之一就是引入 Elon Musk 来领导一个旨在削减政府开支的任务小组。

sentences.en: This was, in many ways, a continuation of his earlier pledge to “drain the swamp”, but now it seemed less politically-motivated, more about using taxpayer money more efficiently and for American interests rather than targeting career politicians.
sentences.zh: 从许多方面来看，这是他早期“清淤泥”承诺的延续，但现在它看起来更少一些政治动机，更多的是关于如何更高效地利用纳税人的钱服务于美国利益，而不是针对职业政客。

sentences.en: And sure enough, Trump was re-elected, and on his first day in office, he signed an Executive Order establishing the Department of Governmental Efficiency - DOGE, for short.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，特朗普成功连任，并在上任第一天签署了一项行政令，成立了政府效率部——简称 DOGE。

sentences.en: As you might know, the acronym DOGE is somewhat of a joke.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能知道的那样，DOGE 这个缩写多少有点开玩笑的意味。

sentences.en: Doge was an early internet meme–a picture of a Japanese shiba inu dog with some text on it–and there was even a cryptocurrency called Dogecoin, which was the first “meme coin”.
sentences.zh: Doge 是早期的互联网表情包——一张带有文字的日本柴犬图片——甚至还有一种叫做狗狗币（Dogecoin）的加密货币，它是第一个“表情包币”。

sentences.en: After Musk and Trump floated the idea of a “government efficiency commission,” a user on X suggested the acronym “DOGE,” and that was it.
sentences.zh: 在 Musk 和特朗普抛出“政府效率委员会”的想法后，X 上的一位用户建议使用“DOGE”这个缩写，事情就这么定下来了。

sentences.en: It might have seemed like a joke, a flippant idea created at a dinner party and hastily turned into reality, but there was a lot of planning that went into it.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是一个笑话，是一个在晚宴上产生、草率付诸现实的轻率想法，但其中其实包含了很多筹划。

sentences.en: The first question was about how to structure this department, or commission.
sentences.zh: 第一个问题是如何构建这个部门或委员会。

sentences.en: A government clearly isn’t like a company with a CEO, who can create and dismantle departments and positions at will.
sentences.zh: 政府显然不像一家拥有 CEO 的公司，CEO 可以随意创建和解散部门和职位。

sentences.en: There are systems of checks and balances, laws in place to prevent a rogue actor from coming in and making sweeping changes that are not in the best interests of the country.
sentences.zh: 这里存在制衡体系，有法律来防止不法分子进来做出不符合国家最大利益的重大改变。

sentences.en: So Musk and his team had to get creative.
sentences.zh: 因此，Musk 和他的团队必须发挥创意。

sentences.en: Instead of creating an entirely new department, which would have been fraught with legal and political issues, they took an existing department, renamed it and expanded its remit.
sentences.zh: 他们没有创建一个全新的部门（这会引发严重的法律和政治问题），而是接管了一个现有的部门，将其改名并扩大了职权范围。

sentences.en: The United States Digital Service, or USDS, was created in 2014 under Barack Obama, and was intended to, and I’m quoting directly, "deliver better government services to the American people through technology and design."
sentences.zh: 美国数字服务局（USDS）于 2014 年在巴拉克·奥巴马执政期间成立，其目的是（我直接引述）“通过技术和设计为美国人民提供更好的政府服务。”

sentences.en: The Executive Order signed by Trump on his first day in office renamed it as the United States DOGE Service, which conveniently meant it could still have the same initials: USDS.
sentences.zh: 特朗普在上任第一天签署的行政令将其重新命名为美国 DOGE 服务局，这刚好意味着它仍然可以使用相同的首字母缩写：USDS。

sentences.en: And within the renamed and reorganised USDS sat DOGE: the Department of Governmental Efficiency.
sentences.zh: 在这个更名和重组的 USDS 内部，便是 DOGE：政府效率部。

sentences.en: Now, it still isn’t completely clear what the difference between the USDS and DOGE is, and there are several other agencies that sit under or alongside it.
sentences.zh: 目前，USDS 和 DOGE 之间的区别仍然不是很清晰，还有其他几个机构隶属于它或与它并列。

sentences.en: In the interests of simplicity, I’ll call them all DOGE going forward.
sentences.zh: 为了简单起见，我接下来统称它们为 DOGE。

sentences.en: And DOGE had big plans. In late October of 2024, shortly before the election, Elon Musk had claimed that he could cut the federal budget by at least $2 trillion, around one-third of its total.
sentences.zh: DOGE 拥有宏伟的计划。在 2024 年 10 月下旬，即大选前不久，Elon Musk 曾声称他可以削减至少 2 万亿美元的联邦预算，大约占总预算的三分之一。

sentences.en: Importantly, $2 trillion is higher than the discretionary spending budget.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，2 万亿美元高于可自由支配支出预算。

sentences.en: Now, to explain why this is important, in the United States, federal government spending is split into three categories: mandatory spending, discretionary spending, and interest on government debt.
sentences.zh: 为了解释为什么这很重要，在美国，联邦政府支出分为三类：强制性支出、可自由支配支出以及政府债务利息。

sentences.en: Mandatory spending refers to the money that the government is obligated to spend on its citizens, including programs such as Social Security and Medicare.
sentences.zh: 强制性支出是指政府有义务花在公民身上的资金，包括社会保障和医疗保险等项目。

sentences.en: Interest on government debt is the interest the US government pays on its bonds, which it is obliged to pay to maintain faith in the US dollar.
sentences.zh: 政府债务利息是指美国政府为其债券支付的利息，这是维护美元信誉所必须支付的。

sentences.en: Discretionary spending is the only category that is “optional”, which can be increased or decreased by Congress.
sentences.zh: 可自由支配支出是唯一的“可选”类别，可以由国会增加或减少。

sentences.en: This includes things like defence, foreign aid, transportation and education.
sentences.zh: 这包括国防、对外援助、交通和教育等方面。

sentences.en: Mandatory spending is around 60% of the total, discretionary spending is 27%, and the remaining 13% is interest on government debt.
sentences.zh: 强制性支出约占总额的 60%，可自由支配支出占 27%，剩下的 13% 是政府债务利息。

sentences.en: Together, it makes up almost $7 trillion per year, and there was Musk claiming he could trim this to more like $5 trillion.
sentences.zh: 加起来每年将近 7 万亿美元，而 Musk 却声称他能将其削减到接近 5 万亿美元。

sentences.en: Now, there were few people who would claim that the US government was this slick, well-oiled machine that was as efficient as it could be.
sentences.zh: 现在，几乎没有人会说美国政府是一个精简、运转良好且达到最高效率的机器。

sentences.en: Of course, there was waste, of course, there were people who weren’t working particularly hard.
sentences.zh: 当然存在浪费，当然也有人工作并不算特别努力。

sentences.en: Perhaps there were some people who weren’t doing any work at all.
sentences.zh: 也许有些人根本什么都没干。

sentences.en: We’re talking about millions of people, a vast bureaucracy, a government.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论的是数百万人口、一个庞大的官僚机构和一个政府。

sentences.en: A little waste was to be expected. But to say that 30% of government spending was wasteful, especially given that such a large amount of government spending is mandatory, with the money going to people the government is legally required to give it to, that seemed extreme.
sentences.zh: 出现一点浪费是可以预料的。但要说 30% 的政府支出都是浪费，考虑到其中很大一部分政府支出是强制性的，这些钱是法律规定政府必须支付给人们的，这就显得有些极端了。

sentences.en: But Elon Musk, even to his greatest critics, had an established track record of pushing through change that was thought to be impossible, whether it was Twitter, mass-market electric cars or reusable rockets.
sentences.zh: 但即便面对最严厉的批评者，Elon Musk 在强行推行被认为是不可能实现的变革方面也有着既定的记录，无论是 Twitter、大众市场电动汽车还是可回收火箭。

sentences.en: And almost immediately, DOGE got to work.
sentences.zh: DOGE 几乎立刻就开始了工作。

sentences.en: It was purposefully kept small, with teams of one team lead, one engineer, one HR specialist and one lawyer.
sentences.zh: 它被刻意保持在很小的规模，每个团队由一名团队负责人、一名工程师、一名 HR 专家和一名律师组成。

sentences.en: These DOGE teams were placed within federal agencies, but instead of a traditional, consultant-led approach, the problem of increasing efficiency was attacked from a technical angle.
sentences.zh: 这些 DOGE 团队被派驻到联邦机构内部，但他们没有采用传统的、以顾问为主导的方法，而是从技术角度切入来解决提高效率的问题。

sentences.en: Most often, DOGE employees were not previously federal workers, and instead were highly talented, and often very young, computer programmers.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，DOGE 员工以前都不是联邦雇员，而是才华横溢、通常非常年轻的计算机程序员。

sentences.en: They were embedded within government agencies, given access to government computer systems, and allowed to get to work.
sentences.zh: 他们被安插在政府机构内部，获得政府计算机系统的访问权限，并开始工作。

sentences.en: The hypothesis was that by using AI and technical wizardry, DOGE would be able to identify wasteful spending in a way that previous federal systems would not.
sentences.zh: 他们的假设是，通过利用人工智能和技术奇迹，DOGE 将能够以以往联邦系统无法做到的方式识别出浪费的支出。

sentences.en: This huge fraud and waste that some people thought was going on within the US government would have nowhere to hide; it would be identified, stopped, and the savings passed back to the American taxpayer.
sentences.zh: 一些人认为正在美国政府内部发生的这种巨大欺诈和浪费将无处藏身；它们将被识别、制止，并将节省下来的资金返还给美国纳税人。

sentences.en: However, almost immediately, the controversy started.
sentences.zh: 然而，争议几乎立刻就开始了。

sentences.en: At the start of February, reports emerged that DOGE had gained access to the Treasury Department’s payment system, which handles everything from Social Security checks to tax refunds.
sentences.zh: 2 月初，有报道称 DOGE 获得了财政部支付系统的访问权限，该系统处理从社会保障支票到退税的一切事务。

sentences.en: This raised alarm bells. Democratic lawmakers, like Senator Elizabeth Warren, warned that giving an unelected group like DOGE access to such sensitive information was a recipe for disaster.
sentences.zh: 这敲响了警钟。民主党议员（如参议员 Elizabeth Warren）警告称，让像 DOGE 这样未经选举产生的小团体访问如此敏感的信息简直是自取灭亡。

sentences.en: What if there were errors? What if the data was misused?
sentences.zh: 如果出现错误怎么办？如果数据被滥用怎么办？

sentences.en: After all, Musk’s companies, like SpaceX and Tesla, have billions in government contracts.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，Musk 的公司（如 SpaceX 和 Tesla）拥有数十亿美元的政府合同。

sentences.en: Critics, including unions and consumer advocacy groups, cried foul, arguing that this was a massive conflict of interest.
sentences.zh: 包括工会和消费者权益组织在内的批评人士强烈抗议，认为这构成了巨大的利益冲突。

sentences.en: A lawsuit was filed on February 3rd, alleging that DOGE’s access to the Treasury’s systems violated federal privacy laws.
sentences.zh: 2 月 3 日提起了一起诉讼，指控 DOGE 访问财政部系统的行为违反了联邦隐私法。

sentences.en: And then there were the layoffs. DOGE didn’t just want to modernise technology; it wanted to shrink the federal workforce dramatically.
sentences.zh: 接下来就是裁员。DOGE 不仅想实现技术现代化；它还想大幅缩减联邦员工队伍。

sentences.en: By April 2025, DOGE claimed to have saved $150 billion through a combination of contract cancellations, grant terminations, and workforce reductions.
sentences.zh: 到 2025 年 4 月，DOGE 声称通过取消合同、终止赠款和削减员工，已经节省了 150 京（注：此处应为 1500 亿）美元。

sentences.en: But these cuts came at a cost. For example, the Department of Health and Human Services saw 20,000 positions slashed, including roles at the National Institutes of Health, which funds critical medical research.
sentences.zh: 但这些削减是有代价的。例如，卫生与公众服务部有 20,000 个职位被砍掉，其中包括资助关键医学研究的国家卫生研究院的职位。

sentences.en: One analysis estimated that these cuts could lead to a $10 billion loss in economic activity and 44,000 jobs across the country.
sentences.zh: 一项分析估计，这些削减可能导致全美经济活动损失 100 亿美元，并减少 44,000 个工作岗位。

sentences.en: After all, these were 44,000 people, enough to fit a football stadium, who were now out of work, might now depend on the government for assistance, and be radically cutting down their own discretionary spending on all the sort of stuff that keeps the American economy driving forward.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这 44,000 个人（足以塞满一个足球场）现在失业了，他们现在可能要靠政府救济生活，并且会大幅削减他们自己的可自由支配支出——而正是这些支出支撑着美国经济向前发展。

sentences.en: The United States Agency for International Development, or USAID, was hit even harder, with most of its programmes gutted, disbanded completely.
sentences.zh: 美国国际开发署（USAID）受到的打击更为严重，其大部分项目都被彻底废除和解散。

sentences.en: Critics pointed out that these cuts weren’t just about trimming fat; they were dismantling programs that supported vulnerable populations, both at home and abroad.
sentences.zh: 批评人士指出，这些削减不仅仅是为了去除赘肉；它们正在拆除那些支持国内外弱势群体的项目。

sentences.en: By May of 2025, some estimates linked DOGE’s foreign aid cuts to 300,000 deaths, mostly children.
sentences.zh: 到 2025 年 5 月，一些估计将 DOGE 的对外援助削减与 30,0000 起死亡事件联系起来，其中大部分是儿童。

sentences.en: To this, the reaction of Musk and Trump can be summed up as “well, it shouldn’t be up to the American taxpayer to pay for all this stuff.”
sentences.zh: 对此，Musk 和特朗普的反应可以总结为“好吧，不应该由美国纳税人为所有这些东西买单。”

sentences.en: Like it or not, Trump won the election on an America-first mandate, and this was nothing if not America first.
sentences.zh: 不管你喜不喜欢，特朗普是以“美国优先”的纲领赢得大选的，这绝对可以说是货真价实的美国优先。

sentences.en: And alongside this, there were plenty of examples of federal government spending that raised a few eyebrows, even to Trump’s greatest critics.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有很多联邦政府支出的例子让人大跌眼镜，甚至让特朗普最坚定的批评者也感到侧目。

sentences.en: Funding for a transgender medical clinic in India, $20 million to create a Sesame Street show in Iraq, or even the discovery that the US Air Force had been charged $1,300 per reheatable coffee cup by Boeing.
sentences.zh: 为印度的变性人医疗诊所提供资金，斥资 2000 万美元在伊拉克制作《芝麻街》节目，甚至发现美国空军向波音公司购买每个可加热咖啡杯的花费高达 1300 美元。

sentences.en: DOGE’s website proudly displayed a “Wall of Receipts,” listing thousands of terminated contracts and grants, with savings they claimed reached $205 billion by August 2025, a savings of $1,273.29 per taxpayer.
sentences.zh: DOGE 的网站自豪地展示了一面“收据墙”，上面列出了数千份被终止的合同和赠款，并声称截至 2025 年 8 月节省的资金达到了 2050 亿美元，相当于为每个纳税人节省了 1,273.29 美元。

sentences.en: To many Americans, this was refreshing, a government finally taking a hard look at where their tax dollars were going, and, most importantly, acting to fix it.
sentences.zh: 对许多美国人来说，这令人耳目一新：政府终于开始认真审视他们的税款去向，最重要的是，付诸行动来解决问题。

sentences.en: Indeed, a March 2025 NBC poll found that 46% of voters thought DOGE was a good idea in principle.
sentences.zh: 事实上，2025 年 3 月的一项 NBC 民意调查发现，46% 的选民认为 DOGE 原则上是一个好主意。

sentences.en: But the critics weren’t having it. They argued that DOGE’s savings were wildly exaggerated.
sentences.zh: 但批评人士并不买账。他们认为 DOGE 节省的资金被严重夸大了。

sentences.en: Firstly, the $2 trillion figure that was floated in the days before the election was reduced to $1 trillion shortly after DOGE was established, then to $150 billion by April 2025, a reduction of more than 90%.
sentences.zh: 首先，大选前几天抛出的 2 万亿美元数字在 DOGE 成立后不久就被缩减到了 1 万亿美元，接着在 2025 年 4 月降到了 1500 亿美元，缩减幅度超过 90%。

sentences.en: And there were claims that it would actually have a negative effect; there wouldn’t just be no savings, it would end up costing the country money.
sentences.zh: 并且有人声称它实际上会产生负面影响；不仅省不下钱，最后反而会增加国家的开支。

sentences.en: Independent analyses, like one from the Internal Revenue Service, warned that DOGE’s cuts to tax enforcement could actually increase the federal deficit by hundreds of billions, as the IRS would struggle to collect revenue.
sentences.zh: 独立分析机构（例如来自国税局的分析）警告称，DOGE 对税收执法的削减实际上可能会导致联邦赤字增加数千亿美元，因为国税局将难以收回税收。

sentences.en: In other words, these cost “savings” would be more than offset by losses in tax revenue, meaning the country lost, not saved money.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这些成本“节省”将被税收收入的损失完全抵消，这意味着国家不是省了钱，而是亏了钱。

sentences.en: And then there were the accounting errors and “creative” savings calculations.
sentences.zh: 接着是会计错误和“富有创意”的节约计算方法。

sentences.en: Journalists uncovered billions of dollars in miscounting, with some “savings” tied to contracts that had already been cancelled before DOGE even existed, and other “savings” accounting for the absolute maximum that could possibly be spent, and the real number almost always coming in much lower.
sentences.zh: 记者们发现了数十亿美元的计算失误，其中一些“节约”与 DOGE 成立之前就已经取消的合同挂钩，而另一些“节约”则计算了可能花费的绝对最大值，而实际数字几乎总是要低得多。

sentences.en: And then there was what we can characterise as “The Musk Factor”.
sentences.zh: 然后就是我们可以称之为“Musk 因素”的东西。

sentences.en: If DOGE was controversial, its leader was even more so.
sentences.zh: 如果说 DOGE 充满争议，那么它的领导者则更具争议。

sentences.en: Elon Musk, the billionaire behind Tesla, SpaceX, and X, was the face of DOGE, even if he was officially just a “special government employee”, technically only allowed to work 130 days a year.
sentences.zh: Elon Musk，这位特斯拉、SpaceX 和 X 背后的亿万富翁，是 DOGE 的门面，尽管他官方身份只是一名“特殊政府雇员”，技术上每年只被允许工作 130 天。

sentences.en: His involvement was a double-edged sword.
sentences.zh: 他的参与是一把双刃剑。

sentences.en: On one hand, his reputation as a disruptor gave DOGE credibility among those who wanted radical change.
sentences.zh: 一方面，他作为颠覆者的声誉让 DOGE 在那些想要彻底变革的人中间赢得了信誉。

sentences.en: He wasn’t a career politician; he was a modern-day Thomas Edison —a tech genius and entrepreneur who had run wildly successful companies.
sentences.zh: 他不是一个职业政客；他是一位现代的托马斯·爱迪生——一个运营过极其成功的公司的科技天才和企业家。

sentences.en: If anyone was up to the challenge, it was him.
sentences.zh: 如果说有人能胜任这个挑战，那就是他。

sentences.en: On the other hand, Musk’s involvement raised red flags, tainting the project.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，Musk 的参与亮起了红灯，给这个项目抹上了阴影。

sentences.en: His businesses rely heavily on government contracts; SpaceX alone has deals worth billions with NASA and the Department of Defence.
sentences.zh: 他的企业严重依赖政府合同；仅 SpaceX 就与 NASA 和国防部拥有价值数十亿美元的协议。

sentences.en: Critics pointed out that Musk’s access to federal systems could benefit his companies while harming competitors.
sentences.zh: 批评人士指出，Musk 访问联邦系统的权限可能会使他的公司受益，同时损害竞争对手的利益。

sentences.en: He was, after all, being given unfettered access to government systems, something that was perhaps worth hundreds of billions to his companies.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，他被赋予了对政府系统的无限制访问权限，这对于他的公司来说可能价值数千亿美元。

sentences.en: By April 2025, just a few months after DOGE was established, the cracks were starting to show.
sentences.zh: 到 2025 年 4 月，即 DOGE 成立几个月后，裂痕开始显现。

sentences.en: Protests erupted across the country, with chants of “Elon Musk has to go” heard outside Tesla showrooms.
sentences.zh: 全美各地爆发了抗议活动，特斯拉展厅外听到了“Elon Musk 必须下台”的口号声。

sentences.en: In Manhattan, demonstrators waved signs reading “No Trump, No Musk, No Fascist USA.”
sentences.zh: 在曼哈顿，示威者挥舞着写着“不要特朗普，不要马斯克，不要法西斯美国”的标语。

sentences.en: There were organised boycotts of Tesla, Musk’s electric car company.
sentences.zh: 人们组织了对马斯克电动汽车公司特斯拉的抵制活动。

sentences.en: Sales dropped dramatically, most prominently in Europe but also in the US, and this was followed by a crash in the share price.
sentences.zh: 销量急剧下降，在欧洲最为明显，在美国也是如此，随后股价也随之暴跌。

sentences.en: Musk was forced to intervene, and in April, he announced that he would be leaving DOGE to focus on Tesla.
sentences.zh: Musk 被迫进行干预，并在 4 月份宣布他将离开 DOGE 以专注于特斯拉。

sentences.en: By the start of May, he was officially gone.
sentences.zh: 到 5 月初，他已正式离职。

sentences.en: Now, although its creator, and the man most associated with it, is no longer involved, DOGE is still active, and its official mandate runs until July 2026.
sentences.zh: 现在，尽管其创始人和与其联系最紧密的人已经不再参与，但 DOGE 仍在运作，其官方任期将持续到 2026 年 7 月。

sentences.en: So, what does the future hold for DOGE? As of September 2025, although it is not in the news as much as earlier in the year, it’s still an important question.
sentences.zh: 那么，DOGE 的未来会怎样？截至 2025 年 9 月，尽管它不像今年早些时候那样频频登上新闻，但这仍然是一个重要的问题。

sentences.en: President Trump could extend DOGE’s mandate with another executive order, and there’s talk of states like Oklahoma and Texas launching their own DOGE-inspired initiatives.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统可能会通过另一项行政令延长 DOGE 的任期，并且有传言称俄克拉荷马州和德克萨斯州等州正在发起他们自己的受 DOGE 启发的倡议。

sentences.en: Even some European leaders have expressed curiosity about the concept, wondering if a similar approach could work across the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 甚至一些欧洲领导人也对这个概念表达了好奇，想知道类似的方法是否能在跨大西洋彼岸行得通。

sentences.en: But the road ahead is far from smooth. The organisation is still plagued by legal battles.
sentences.zh: 但前方的道路远非一帆风顺。该组织仍然饱受法律诉讼的困扰。

sentences.en: And as for public opinion, it remains split.
sentences.zh: 至于公众舆论，依然存在分歧。

sentences.en: Younger Americans especially disapprove of DOGE, and older, especially Republican-leaning voters, support it.
sentences.zh: 年轻的美国人尤其不赞成 DOGE，而年长的、尤其是倾向于共和党的选民则支持它。

sentences.en: For its supporters, DOGE is a bold experiment in making government leaner and more accountable, a chance to finally tackle the bureaucracy that’s been slowing America down.
sentences.zh: 对于支持者来说，DOGE 是一场让政府更精简、更负责的大胆实验，是一个终于可以着手解决拖慢美国后腿的官僚主义的机会。

sentences.en: For its critics, it is a reckless power grab, one that risks dismantling vital services, eroding public trust, and furthermore, one that looks like it will even cost, not save, the country money.
sentences.zh: 对于批评者来说，这是一场鲁莽的权力争夺，有可能拆除重要服务、侵蚀公众信任，此外，它看起来甚至会让国家赔钱而不是省钱。

sentences.en: Whether it is a stroke of genius or a spectacular misstep, one thing is certain: DOGE has sparked a conversation about what government should be, who it should serve, and how it should be run.
sentences.zh: 无论这是一记神来之笔还是一个巨大的失误，有一点是确定的：DOGE 引发了一场关于政府应该是什么样、它应该服务于谁以及它应该如何运作的讨论。

sentences.en: And that conversation, love it or loathe it, isn’t going away anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 而无论你爱它还是恨它，这场讨论在短期内都不会消失。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on DOGE.
sentences.zh: 好了，以上就是本期关于 DOGE 的节目的全部内容。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目对你有所启发，也希望你学到了新的东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对本期节目的看法。

sentences.en: What do you think of DOGE? Do you think it’s a fantastic idea and that every country should follow its example, that it was a terrible, politicised plot, or somewhere in between?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看 DOGE？你认为这是一个绝妙的主意，每个国家都应该效仿它，还是一个糟糕的、充满政治色彩的阴谋，抑或是介于两者之间？

sentences.en: For the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 对于会员朋友们，你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的头脑畅聊。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
